doc: The one 'in combat' rule (scripts/match/in_combat.gd). A Hunter or a Boki is in combat for window_s seconds after it deals or takes damage in a fight: a hit on or from a Hunter, a Boki, a monster or Blight. Healing, falls, wall slams, heat, friendly fire and damage to yourself don't count. A Boki's fight is its owner's too. Hunter shield refill, a Boki's own mending, the drive music, a Boki's 10 Hz think out of combat and a Boki's refused orders all read it, so they switch on the same frame. (Far bots' 20 Hz step is SimLod's, not this window: far fights are slowed on purpose.) 4 s is the reference tuning's recent-combat mark (the same 4 s its health recovery waits after damage). Channels (a recall, an exit call, a rune, a box revive) are not on this window: the source cancels them on the hit itself, so they read Hunter.hurt_at.
